bug_semantics: The ::import-binfile RPC accepted an optional caller-controlled file-id for in-place v3 import but authorized only the separately supplied project-id. The overwrite branch loaded the target with an id-only get-minimal-file lookup, imported attacker content under the caller's project-id, and updated the existing file row by that id, so an authenticated user who could edit their own project could overwrite and re-parent a victim file. The advisory also mentions WebSocket subscription; the named import-binfile file-id gap and the BIC/fix here are the file-takeover path.
flaw_origin: 37cec8891f44b0c320006193783d8648d3f32d0f is the smallest commit that first wrote the vulnerable path end to end: optional :file-id on schema:import-binfile, assoc of that id onto ::bfc/file-id with no file-level permission check, import-file-and-overwrite* (id-only lookup), and save-file! update-vs-insert when ::overwrite is set while keeping the caller project-id. Direct parent fd62141c04817c2ae86d10ad41b130fe616cf789 had none of those lines and only created new imported files.
